text: Every tool on the agent surface is a read. Amending the canon requires the CLI, run by a person.
Every drafted candidate carries the passage it came from, verbatim, or it is not shown.
There is no --accept-all. A canon adopted wholesale is disengagement at t=0.
Two rules stating different measures are never duplicates.
A canon on the personal profile never renders a verdict and never exits 1.
The record format is CC0 and the tooling is AGPL-3.0-or-later; adopting the format is not a lock-in decision.

rationale: One steward, stated as data rather than only as prose. A grant is how this stops being a notebook.

text: Pull requests are open on every path in this repository. What gates a change is the suite, not a list of permitted directories.
A change lands green or it does not land: rustfmt, clippy with no warnings, and the whole suite, on a clean checkout.
Contributions are licensed under the agreement in CLA.md. In return the project is always also available under an OSI-approved open-source license, and that promise cannot be walked back.
A new op is refused until the census in adequacy_bar names the primitive it serves and the composition that did not reach it. Two domains and a failed composition, or no new op.
A community adds a governance move in the extension half of the op namespace. Nothing a reader must already understand goes in the other half without a version bump.
canon-core takes no dependency that reads a file, opens a socket, or calls a model. The fold's purity is the dependency list, not discipline.
A model call is refused unless the endpoint is on this machine, unless the person running it says otherwise with --allow-remote. Every call prints the endpoint it used.

A fixture is vendored, never depended on across repositories, and carries a PROVENANCE.md naming the upstream commit and the sha256 of every file copied. A standalone clone is the property the whole tool is built around.
A fixture that replays governance ships its positions in the fixture and needs no endpoint. If replaying one requires a model, the split between extraction and decision has been broken.
Every accuracy figure names the model and the endpoint that produced it. A figure whose run predates a change to what it measures is withdrawn, not restated.
Every repository path a narrative document cites must resolve. docs-gate checks it, because a map that is wrong about where things are is worse than no map.
A documentation rule nobody objected to in two weeks is a rule. The cost of an unanswered doc proposal should fall on the steward, not the person who wrote it.

rationale: SPEC v2 already split the op namespace so a community can add a governance move without every other implementation changing. A plugin API would be a second way to do the same thing, and the one that can break somebody else's reader.

about: a bot that closes stale issues
rationale: An unanswered issue is the maintainer's debt, not the reporter's. Closing it on a timer hides the debt instead of paying it.

It needs an endpoint and a model whose numbers move between runs. A gate that goes red for the weather teaches people to ignore gates. The bars run by hand and every number is published with the model that produced it.

text: Nobody has decided what earns a grant. A second person holding standing over a scope is the next real governance event and there is no rule for it.
What is the bar for merging a fixture whose source cannot be redistributed?
Who holds standing over canon.format once a second implementation of the format exists? The format is CC0 and this canon governs only this repository's copy of it.

Every accuracy figure names the resolved model that produced it, never an alias, and the endpoint it was served from. An alias is not provenance: `primary` moved from a 27B to a 35B MoE on 2026-08-30, and every figure recorded against the name alone became a figure about nothing. A run whose measurement changed under it is withdrawn, not restated.
rationale: As drafted this was satisfied by `model: primary`, which is the exact case STUDY.md already flags as broken. DEMO_PLAN.md had already decided it in prose — an alias is not provenance — and the canon was stating something weaker than the project practices.

text: Every repository path a narrative document links to must resolve. docs-gate checks it. Backticked paths in prose are deliberately not checked — most are shorthand rather than citations, and a gate whose false positives outnumber its catches is one people learn to ignore.
rationale: 'cites' claimed more than the gate enforces: 83 of 91 backticked repo-ish paths in this tree do not resolve as written, and nearly all of them are legitimate prose.

text: The fold takes ts_unix and actor as given. What defends the ledger is whoever may append to the file: git in a repository, the household on a shared folder. Neither is canon's, and canon says so rather than pretending to be it. canon guard is the second-order tool, outside the format and outside the ledger it guards.

about: identity and time inside the format
rationale: An account system is the thing this project refuses, and a signing key still needs somebody outside canon to bind it to a person. A timestamp the fold could verify would need a clock the fold does not have. Both stay the substrate's: signed commits and branch protection where the ledger lives in git, mutual visibility where it lives on a shared folder. canon guard git wires the first; nothing wires the second.

text: The fold takes ts_unix as given, and takes actor as given only for a name that has not bound a key. What defends the ledger beyond that is whoever may append to the file: git in a repository, the household on a shared folder. canon guard is the second-order tool, outside the format and outside the ledger it guards.
rationale: A name can now bind a key; see docs/SIGNING_DESIGN.md.
Identity is in the format now, opt-in per name: a person binds their own key and the group checks fingerprints out of band. See docs/SIGNING_DESIGN.md.
A timestamp the fold could verify would need a clock the fold does not have. Signing decides by content, never by ts_unix.
